description: YTsaurus is a scalable and fault-tolerant open-source big data platform.
vibe: Map the monorepo, enforce branch hygiene, and let the style guides do the talking.
highlights: Branch naming is treated as a hard upstream contract enforced by branch protection.
The repository is mapped at a granular level, especially the many server components under `yt/yt/server/`.
Third-party code is explicitly separated into `contrib/` and `vendor/` to keep ownership boundaries clear.
Language-specific style guides are delegated to `yt/styleguide/cpp.md` and `yt/styleguide/python.md` rather than duplicated.
The file prioritizes navigability and onboarding over prescribing implementation details.
assessment: This is a pragmatic navigation and convention file for a very large monorepo. Its strength is reducing ambiguity around branch naming and repository layout, which matters when many contributors and Copilot suggestions touch different subsystems. It is less an engineering-taste manifesto and more a map plus hard branch-hygiene rule, so it avoids over-prescribing code patterns while still enforcing one critical workflow constraint.
